Body center around (380, 270), ellipse rx 85 ry 65, tilted. Neck goes forward-up to head around (500, 200), beak long pointing forward-down to (640, 230) with pouch.

Wing on body, folded, maybe one wing reaching to handlebar.

Feet on pedals: pedal crank at bottom bracket (405,430), crank radius 32. Pedal positions: (437, 455) and (373, 405). Legs from body down to pedals.

Let me build carefully with nice colors: pelican plumage white/cream with grey accents, beak orange/yellow with pink pouch. Bicycle teal/coral retro.

Use <defs> with a symbol for wheel? Symbols can't easily be reused with different positions... they can via <use x= y=>. Let's define a wheel group in defs with center at 0,0 and use with transform translate. That's clean.

Wheel: r_tire = 78, tire stroke 10, rim r=64 stroke 5, spokes r=62, hub r=9.

answer:
Here's a cheerful pelican out for a bike ride — hand‑built SVG, no external assets, scales cleanly.

```svg
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 800 600" width="800" height="600"
     role="img" aria-label="A pelican wearing a helmet and scarf riding a teal bicycle along a country road">
  <title>Pelican Riding a Bicycle</title>
  <desc>A white pelican with a long orange pouched beak, crimson helmet and golden scarf, pedalling a teal road bike.</desc>

  <defs>
    <linearGradient id="sky" x1="0" y1="0" x2="0" y2="1">
      <stop offset="0"   stop-color="#93dcf2"/>
      <stop offset=".55" stop-color="#cdeef4"/>
      <stop offset="1"   stop-color="#fdf1d8"/>
    </linearGradient>
    <radialGradient id="sunG" cx=".5" cy=".5" r=".5">
```
